steps.tx: **Treatment-resistant schizophrenia** is diagnosed when a patient demonstrates persistent moderate to severe psychotic symptoms despite at least two adequate trials of different antipsychotic agents. Each trial must utilize therapeutic doses equivalent to at least 600 milligrams of chlorpromazine daily for a minimum duration of six continuous weeks.
steps.say: Treatment resistance requires failure of two adequate trials of different antipsychotics at therapeutic doses for at least six weeks each. Clozapine is the gold standard therapy.

vis.alt: Clozapine atypical receptor binding and surveillance protocols
vis.caption: Atypical antipsychotic mechanisms showing clozapine multi-receptor affinity, agranulocytosis risk, and adverse effect profile.

steps.tx: **Atypical receptor pharmacology of clozapine** features high affinity for dopamine D4, serotonin 5-HT2A, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, alongside exceptionally weak binding to striatal D2 receptors. Because striatal D2 occupancy remains below 60 percent, clozapine virtually never induces extrapyramidal symptoms or tardive dyskinesia.
steps.say: Clozapine exhibits potent D4 and 5-HT2A antagonism with minimal striatal D2 blockade. It avoids extrapyramidal motor side effects and does not cause tardive dyskinesia.

left.title: Receptor Affinities
points: Antagonist at H1 and alpha-1 receptors

steps.tx: **Agranulocytosis monitoring protocol** mandates baseline absolute neutrophil count exceeding 1500 per microliter before initiating clozapine therapy. Blood counts are performed weekly for the first 18 weeks, fortnightly from week 19 through week 52, and every four weeks indefinitely thereafter to intercept life-threatening bone marrow suppression.
steps.say: Absolute neutrophil counts must exceed 1500 per microliter before therapy. Monitoring is weekly for eighteen weeks, fortnightly until one year, and monthly thereafter.

nodes.label: Baseline ANC >= 1500/mcL (>=1000 in benign ethnic neutropenia)
Fortnightly ANC monitoring from week 19 to week 52

steps.tx: **Absolute neutrophil count thresholds** dictate immediate clinical action: a count dropping between 1000 and 1499 per microliter requires three-times-weekly monitoring. An absolute neutrophil count falling below 1000 per microliter mandates immediate, permanent clozapine cessation, strict infectious disease consultation, and protective isolation.
steps.say: Counts between 1000 and 1499 require blood tests three times weekly. A drop below 1000 per microliter demands immediate and permanent clozapine discontinuation.

vis.title: ANC Action Cutoffs
rows: Continue clozapine; test ANC three times weekly
Stop clozapine immediately; daily haematology monitoring
Stop clozapine permanently; reverse barrier nursing, consider G-CSF

steps.tx: **Adverse effects of clozapine** include dose-dependent seizure risk exceeding five percent at doses over 600 milligrams daily, profound sedation, severe constipation, significant metabolic syndrome, and nocturnal hypersalivation. Fatal myocarditis occurs predominantly during the initial month of titration, requiring baseline electrocardiography and serial cardiac troponin monitoring.
steps.say: Clozapine can induce dose-related seizures, sedation, severe constipation, metabolic syndrome, and hypersalivation. Acute myocarditis usually presents during the first month of therapy.

vis.title: Non-Haematological Complications
rows: Baseline troponin & ECG; stop immediately if elevated
Titrate slowly; add sodium valproate above 450 mg/day
Prophylactic stimulant laxatives to avoid paralytic ileus
Sublingual ipratropium spray or oral glycopyrrolate

steps.tx: **Depot antipsychotic formulations**, such as haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, and paliperidone palmitate, resolve covert medication non-adherence in non-compliant schizophrenia patients. These long-acting injectable agents require an oral test dose before administration to ensure immunological tolerance and absence of acute dystonic hypersensitivity.
steps.say: Long-acting depot antipsychotics overcome medication non-adherence. An oral test dose is always administered first to confirm patient tolerance and prevent acute dystonia.

steps.tx: Blood count rules govern one antipsychotic, but missed tablets are a different failure of treatment. **Depot antipsychotic formulations**, such as haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, and paliperidone palmitate, remove covert non adherence in schizophrenia. These long acting injections are not started without a precaution. An oral test dose is given first to confirm immunological tolerance and to show that an acute dystonic reaction will not occur. Only after that test is the depot administered.
steps.say: Haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, and paliperidone palmitate are long acting injections for schizophrenia when oral doses are missed in secret. An oral test dose comes first to confirm tolerance and to avoid acute dystonia. The depot is given only after that test.

steps.tx: **Anti-suicidal efficacy of clozapine** represents a unique pharmacological benefit, demonstrating significant reductions in completed suicide and deliberate self-harm in patients with schizophrenia. Clozapine remains the sole psychotropic agent specifically indicated by regulatory authorities for reducing suicidal behavior in chronic psychotic illness.
steps.say: Clozapine reduces completed suicide and severe self-harm in schizophrenia. It is specifically approved for suicide prevention in refractory psychotic illness.

steps.tx: **Therapeutic drug monitoring of clozapine** optimizes clinical response while avoiding toxic neurotoxicity, targeting a trough plasma concentration between 350 and 600 nanograms per milliliter. Plasma levels above 1000 nanograms per milliliter dramatically increase epileptogenic activity without conferring additional therapeutic benefit.
steps.say: Trough plasma clozapine levels should measure between 350 and 600 nanograms per milliliter. Levels above 1000 nanograms markedly heighten seizure probability.
